mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate over the past 3 months indicates an active monetary easing policy that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS declines for 3 consecutive months, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.2% in a single month, it signals deteriorating labor market conditions that reduce consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 5.2% in a month, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential investment (RSAFS) and housing starts (HOUST) indicates a weakening housing market that contracts consumer demand, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS and HOUST decline in past month
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when both RSAFS and HOUST decline, or Rank IC for interaction signal is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: During early recession regimes (INDPRO < 100), declining industrial production signals manufacturing contraction that reduces corporate profitability, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year rolling windows.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% annually signals persistent inflation that triggers monetary policy tightening, reducing equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 2.5% annually, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over 2-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: When non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month, it indicates strong labor market conditions that boost consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when PAYEMS exceeds 200,000, or Rank IC falls below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals monetary tightening coinciding with supply contraction, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS increases and INDPRO declines in past month
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS rises and INDPRO falls, or Rank IC for interaction signal is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle demand slowdown regimes (GDPC1 annualized growth < 1.5%), a decline in residential investment (RSAFS) indicates further consumer demand contraction, predicting negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when GDPC1 < 1.5% and RSAFS declines, or Rank IC for interaction signal is below 0.03 over 3-year windows.
